description_en: A stone memorial pillar from approx. 14th century.The pillar lies 50 meters north of the Patharnauli reservoir (DLK0160), on the eastern side of the road.The pillar is of the same type as others erected in the Dailekh district during the 14th century. The upper part is composed of two horizontal registers of egg-shaped patterns (āmalaka), separated by one plain rounded register. A bulb is carved on top. The lower part is of quadrangular section, with a central, slightly larger part that would usually contain an inscription.Stone pillars were erected throughout the Karnali Basin from the 13th to the 17th century. They are installed to honor the memory of deceased persons, mostly warriors. No inscription could be found that would indicate the identity of the deceased person or the date of installation. It is nevertheless possible to date this pillar from around the 1330's-1340's, based on its typoology, identical to dated pillars from the nearby site of Sātkhambā (DLK0190).
